$comment: The single definition of every version we track upstream. A Dockerfile ARG, a seam manifest, a peerDependency and a release manifest that each carried their own copy meant 'bump the pin' was four edits and one of them was always missed. Tests assert every derived copy equals the value here; the nightly compatibility matrix is one job that loops over these keys.

dsh.notes: First release candidate of the 0.1.2 line (npm `latest` and `next` since 2026-09-03). Adopted on the criterion in decision #25 — probed against the running binary of that version plus our own battery green — not on the tag. Measured before adopting: the published closures of 0.1.2-alpha.5 and 0.1.2-rc.1 are byte-identical across all 224 `@deepseek-ai/*` packages except one version string in `dsh-client-ui-sidebar`, so rc.1 is alpha.5 retagged and the wire, the seams and the profile are unchanged. Subpackage `latest` dist-tags mostly still point at 0.0.1-rc.1, so every install writes an exact version and the peer ranges are declared explicitly. `dsh plugin` manages a profile with pnpm and writes a pnpm-workspace.yaml listing the profile itself, which pnpm 9 refuses to add into without -w; this pin tracks DSH's own packageManager, not the workspace's. Upstream also tags prereleases on GitHub that npm never receives, so the matrix reports the GitHub tag as `upstreamTag` beside the npm `latest`: npm is what is installable and what `behind` means, the tag is the early warning.

openlist.notes: Self-hosted drive aggregator; v4.2.6 (2026-09-01), including access-control and authentication fixes from the current stable release. EviMed uses the pinned list, get and link contracts, then reads bytes through OpenList's same-origin proxy without following a provider-controlled redirect. The service runs with an isolated data volume and tenant-prefixed paths.

mineru.notes: Document parsing for CJK layout, tables and formulas; PyPI 3.4.5. `pypdf` stays as the fast plain-text fallback.

openviking.notes: The one recall index of the base stack: it ranks both the research-memory records and the capsule facts, whose authoritative rows stay in the control-plane PostgreSQL. Never a record store — its `write` offers replace/append/create and no compare-and-swap, so the `expectedVersion` the record store enforces has no equivalent and two concurrent edits of one record would silently lose one. `embedding` is what `scripts/ops/configure-production-state.mjs` renders into the server's ov.conf (provider `dashscope` with `input: "text"`, which appends `/compatible-mode/v1` to `apiBase` itself and is the only provider that sends `dimensions`); changing the model or the dimension invalidates every stored vector, so it takes a `pnpm rebuild:memory-index --all`. `rerank` is read by the control plane, not by the server: `/search/find` never reranks and `/search/search`, which does, navigates by directory abstracts no VLM generates here and returns nothing for this layout, so the reranker runs where the hydrated text already is and the ov.conf carries no rerank section. Both model ids are configuration until a live DashScope check settles them; no key existed when they were written. The server is AGPL-3.0 and runs unmodified as its own service; the CLI, plugins and examples are Apache-2.0. The container tag carries a `v` prefix (`ghcr.io/volcengine/openviking:v0.4.19`) while the PyPI version does not; the unprefixed tag simply does not exist and a compose file that names it fails at pull. Releases land every few days and have moved data layouts before (0.3.x needed a staged migration through 0.4.5; 0.4.18 changed ACL fields from boolean to string), so the pin moves only through the matrix. `@openviking/dsh-memory-plugin` is listed for the local `evimed-web` profile only: it spawns an MCP proxy that talks to the server directly, which the hosted runtime may not do.
